shouldFix.title: The DR-125 activation gate on matrix authoring is absent, though the pinned candidate records it in a dedicated field and D-007 routes it by name
shouldFix.finding: v13's matrixShape carries a field named dr125ActivationGate reading 'OPEN. Owner: DR-125. Divergence owner: the DR-125 successor, not this artifact. Matrix authoring waits on that closure or its disposition.' Its capabilityBoundary says the same in prose: DR-125 is OPEN and 'that closure is an activation gate for matrix authoring (D-007 OBS-D007-T2-02)'. D-007's own entry routes OBS-T2-02, the manifest/DR-125 dual boundary, to those closure acts. DR-125's live row is OPEN. The join never mentions DR-125 — the string occurs zero times — and OBL-MATRIX-CORPUS grounds the matrix and corpus leftover on D-007 and file 02 without recording that the authoring is gated on another row closing first.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The concrete harm is in proposedLaterWork, which invites 'a later D-000 cycle may author the digest-pinned matrix and corpus' with no precondition. A cycle taking that invitation would hit an activation gate the join never named. Preventing exactly that is what a leftover join is for. The omission is also selective rather than a scope boundary: the join does carry the two other cross-row dependencies from the same sources, DR-119 at OBL-G14-DR119 and DR-006 at OBL-DR006-RIDES, and the one it drops is the one the pinned candidate states with the most force, as its own named field.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing false is asserted — matrix and corpus authoring is leftover whether or not it is also gated — and the eligibility conclusion is unaffected, since three leftover obligations hold gates 2 and 3 shut regardless. The gate governs when the leftover can be worked, not whether it is leftover.
shouldFix.repair: Add an obligation in the shape of OBL-G14-DR119 — for example OBL-DR125-ACTIVATION, leftoverDesign false, existingGate 'none on DR-118. Activation gate at DR-125', rideStanding activation-gate-at-DR-125 — citing v13's dr125ActivationGate and D-007's OBS-T2-02, add it to deferredOrRidesElsewhere, add 'Does not retarget DR-125' to the doesNot list, and qualify the matrix-authoring item in proposedLaterWork with the precondition that DR-125 closes or is disposed.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Grading the DR-125 omission a blocker
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: It changes no classification and no eligibility conclusion; it changes what a later act would believe about sequencing. That is the same weight I gave the DR-116 omission at DR-104 and the actor-join omission at DR-105, both graded SHOULD-FIX, and consistency matters more here than severity.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Charging the collapse of v13's OBL-2 through OBL-6 into a single OBL-D007-STRUCTURE obligation
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: I traced each of the seven v13 obligations into the join and all are reachable — role list, matrix, goldens, baseline, known limitations, no-silent-fallback and thresholds. Grouping the five structure fragments that D-007 decided together, under the decision that decided them, is a defensible shape rather than a lost member.

independence.priorParticipation: New row for me. The method that found this finding is the one this series has taught in both directions: enumerate the pinned sources' own inventories before reading the subject's account of them. I read D-007's routed observations, D-113's recording, v13's obligation decomposition, thresholds block, g13g14 block and matrixShape, and the live G13, G14 and DR-125 rows, before assessing the join's obligations. Three of those enumerations came back clean; matrixShape did not.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Fifteen attacks run, one landed, and the repair is additive. Custody holds: subject 4a2cf4d3 at 0444 unmoved with dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left c2b77f6, file 08 at 3a9442d1 equal to the subject's own pin, governing tree clean, and all four cited files reproduce including v13 at the digest D-113 pins. Most of this is right, and two parts are better than right. The Class B token handling is correct and is the inverse of the two joins immediately before it — DR-118's live cell opens with DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, so leftover-design/OPEN against this row is a finding, and the member is keyed leftoverDesignOpenStanding rather than the contradictory name Codex charged at DR-105. The G13 treatment is the most precise in this series: G13's live harness cell says reserved, not named, G13 appears nowhere in the condition-4 cell, and OBL-G13-RESERVED carries an empty namedIdentifiersNotAuthored list, which is exactly right because unlike G09, G12 and G21 there is no named identifier for G13 to be unauthored. Both gate owners are byte-exact, all seven of v13's obligations are reachable in the join, no number is minted anywhere, and all five cited travelling advisory ids occur in D-113's adopted entry. The objection is a missing cross-row dependency. v13 carries a field literally named dr125ActivationGate reading 'OPEN. Owner: DR-125 ... Matrix authoring waits on that closure or its disposition', its capabilityBoundary says the same in prose citing D-007 OBS-D007-T2-02, D-007's entry routes that observation by name, and DR-125's live row is OPEN. The join mentions DR-125 zero times, and OBL-MATRIX-CORPUS treats matrix and corpus authoring as leftover without recording that it is gated on another row closing first. The harm is concrete: proposedLaterWork invites a later cycle to author the matrix with no precondition, and that cycle would hit a gate the join never named. The omission is selective rather than principled, because the join does carry the two other cross-row dependencies from the same sources, DR-119 and DR-006, and drops the one the pinned candidate states most forcefully. I graded it SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker on the same reasoning I applied to the DR-116 omission at DR-104 and the actor-join omission at DR-105: nothing false is asserted and DR-118 stays ineligible either way, so what is understated is the sequencing, not the standing.
